tips.comment: A Simon & Ed Crisford trained 3-year-old who has had 4 races all on the all-weather, winning once and has finished 3rd twice. His win came here at Southwell in a class 5 novice stakes over 6f when made odds-on favorite, leading over 2 furlongs out to win by 2 3/4 lengths. He is in a class 3 handicap over 6f and has Darry Davis in the saddle for the first time. He was tried in a class 2 handicap 9 days ago at Newcastle over 6f where he was denied a clear run from over 2 furlongs out, finishing 12th of the 14 runners beaten 4 3/4 lengths. He is a course and distance winner and the jockey in the saddle has ridden 6 winners in the last 2 weeks. Has a decent shout in this race today.

Won with plenty in hand but hadn't gone unnoticed as he went off 1/5 fav in a maiden at Southwell. Moves into handicap company today off a mark of 82, but there may be plenty of progression to come and should be competitive here.
4/1, creditable sixth of 11 in handicap at Kempton (6f) 20 days ago. Much respected on his Tapeta debut. This really could run well today and I think it is a good price.
Not overused colt who ran well on 4/11 at Kempton over today's trip 3 weeks ago. He was doing his best to catch the leaders and was impeded, which suggests that he has more to come.

Distance winner who’s turned out again quickly after running only 19 days ago but will strip fitter for it as it was first outing since last October. Finished a decent 4th of 9 on that latest run keeping on at the finish of 6f on good ground. Runs off the same rating but with a jockey change on first AW run.

Shaped better than the bare result when placed off this mark on the final run of the season. Met trouble in running when going well and then again inside the final furlong. So, with a clear run and as long as he handles the surface, must have a decent chance here.

Three of her five starts last season came in Group 3 company, not beaten far in a hugely competitive York handicap on her only start in this company. This is her AW debut, but it is also the softest race that she has run in since making a winning debut. That suggests that fresh should be no concern for her.

Has 1 win and 3 frame finishes from 5 starts last year, including a win over 7f at Newcastle on the penultimate start last September. Open to plenty of improvement as a 3-year-old and should run well.

Well, we know he's trained on, and we know he likes the AW. The win last time at Nottingham hinted he is still on the upgrade, having fought off challengers to eventually win with reasonable comfort. The trainer historically does well at this time of year with his AW runners, and this is his only AW runner today.

Winner at Newcastle at this distance at 1 lb lower than today. Mark was raised by 2 lb but was only a length off the winner at this course, having been squeezed for room in the final furlong. Jockey seems to get a tune out of the horse and is fairly treated by the handicapper.

Bonnie's Boy is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Richard Fahey. He was 2nd in 3 of 5 starts as a 2-year-old. He was gelded during his absence. Drawn wide and has a bit to prove but has posted a career high RPR of 81 but is related to three individual winners and out of a very useful dam 5/23 wins and posted a career high RPR of 108 and improved with racing from a mark of 65 to 108 - Richard Fahey has also landed 17 winners in 6f handicaps at Southwell.

Naana's Diamond represents the stable of Alice Haynes. She has one win on her record. This is quite a risky bet considering the fact that she is making her handicap debut and at the same time making her debut on the AW surface. Positive factors include good performances as a 2-year-old and a good draw. At these odds, this each-way bet could become profitable.
Last chance saloon with this one. If he cannot win from this mark, then no more! Now dropped to his lowest ever mark, money is down for him. Should win.

I’m not sure why Rohan keeps being supported when he’s shown that he’s not the force of old while WESTMORIAN is on a huge upward trajectory and searching for a four-timer so should be clear favourite. The son of Holy Roman Emperor did the business for me on Good Friday at Lingfield when coming up in class, but he always looked a danger and I don’t think a 6lb rise in the handicap will hinder him too much. His two wins over C&D came in a cosy fashion and he’s only ran one bad race here so a return to Southwell is a positive. A couple of positive stats for trainer G Tuer boosts claims further; a 25% SR (A/E 1.58) in April and 29% SR (A/E 1.63) with handicappers over 6f at Southwell. 11/2 taken.
Three wins from 12 runs last year and he recorded a career best when landing 7-runner handicap at this course (7.1f) 37 days ago. Can make his presence felt again.

Four runs in 2025 so far and he started off with a win over C&D where he won nicely by 2 lengths before running another good race to finish a close 2nd at Newcastle over 5f when sent off favourite, but he had no luck in running and should've won. They both came in Class 3 races and although his last two runs have been below par, they were in Class 2s and he drops back into Class 3 company here so he looks sure to run a big race off the same mark as his unlucky 2nd at Newcastle three runs ago

A 6-time career winner who won twice last year, including over this CD, and then finished close up and in the frame in 3 of the next 4 starts. Started the new season with an impressive win at Beverley 11 days ago and looks to be improving again this year. A big player despite carrying a 4 lbs penalty.

Going by previous form, leaving out the very last run where BERGERAC met with some trouble, I think he is capable of making his presence felt if running to his earlier form and is considered as a possible placed finisher.

This horse was usually ridden by a jockey with really poor stats (who I personally never back) as a 3-year-old. So the fact that he was able to win on the horse is worth upgrading massively in my eyes. The horse could well prove to have a good season as a 4-year-old and I rate the new jockey. The win in a novice race on debut was when beating a now mid-80s horse. Considering that was this horse's first ever run, you'd have to say a mark of 81 is clearly a winning one. His only run on the AW was a good one too when 2nd at Newcastle.
Did not have the performance desired from new yard LTO when 14th of 19 at Doncaster last month, but just operating 2 lbs above last winning mark and can bounce back in course debut.

The Bell Conductor is an 8-year-old gelding trained by Ivan Furtado and makes his stable debut. He is 8/29 wins, so he knows how to get the job done and is 5/11 wins on the AW with form figures at Southwell of 1-1-1-5-13-1. He returns from a break, but he has won after 88-70 day absences. Ivan Furtado is his fourth stable, having been with Paul Midgley, Phillip Makin, and Craig Lidster, and he has won races with all previous stables. So a change of surroundings could be an omen at 28-1.
Caballo De Mar is on a hat trick here and doesn't look like they've stopped improving. Still off a low weight compared to others in the race. Can win again here.
Surprised that Manxman is not the favorite in this race. A previous course and distance winner, he was beaten by a nose in the Cesarewitch latest. Should do well.

Yet another success story for James Owen, landing another race in C&D handicap in March. Creditable second of 7 in handicap at Newbury (16.5f, good, 3/1) 16 days ago, no match for unexposed rival who was allowed the run of things. One to consider.
Ran to form, beaten one and a half lengths off 78 over 1m6f here last time. Consistent, up in trip will suit. Last run good as 174-day break, so will come on for that. Each way chance.

Kyle Of Lochaish has been running well lately without winning, finishing 3rd in 4 of its last 5 starts. It was also a winner the start prior to that at Salisbury. So, with a little improvement, it could win this race.

A 5-time winner on the flat over staying trips for the previous yard but has not transferred that form to hurdles for Alan King. However, it is well proven over this trip on the flat and has won at this track, so a big run is on the cards.

DUKE OF OXFORD has a chance of going close here. He ran 4th of 14 in his return recently and should strip a lot fitter for that. Connections have put a claimer on board to offset the handicap mark of 96 - he won two starts ago off 92. I think this is a good each way bet.

Seems to be progressing with a couple of wins in the last 6 and a 3rd last time at NCS. Has been raised again, albeit only slightly, but the handicappers must be exercised at least, which can be a good sign.

Good run from the 6yo mare three weeks ago, beaten around a length in a 13-runner contest. A wide draw saw her coming from the rear that day. It was her first run after a 5-month break and she can improve for it. Just 1 win last year but plenty of near misses while rated much higher than her current mark. Good jockey booking for this apprentice riders’ handicap and he can still claim a very useful 7lb.

Mr Nippy hails from the strong Johnston yard and they were successful in this race last year with Zabeel Road. Always have their debutantes forward and they will be looking for a repeat here in a similarly small field.

The 4yo has 2 wins from 11. Lightly raced last year, struggled off a high mark but he was 3rd over this 10f C/D last summer off a 10lb higher mark. He had a wind op over the winter. Far too keen four weeks ago on the AW on his return from a 6 month break, and hampered late on when still in the mix. Worth another chance in this weak looking contest.

The 4yo enjoyed the return to turf two weeks ago, after a spell on the AW. He was a good 3rd of 13 over this 7f trip. The three runners around him at the finish were rated 84, 86, and 87. He now faces rivals rated 61-74 and is 5lb better off at the weights with a good apprentice booked for the ride.
RED MIRAGE has a good record fresh and has dropped to 3lb below his last winning mark. Looks well-worth an each way bet at the price with this maybe the best time to catch him.

A competitive-looking handicap where a chance is taken on Count Palatine, who looks a lot less exposed than others here. He ran well a couple of weeks back at Thirsk after 6 months off and will be all the fitter for that run. Most of his better form is on top of the ground, which he gets here.

Four career runs for the 3yo filly. She was an impressive winner on her handicap debut last week, winning the 15 runner contest by 5L, eased down at the finish. A 6lb higher mark might not stop her in this contest.

The lightly raced 4yo filly finished last year in good form, two wins and two near misses - four good RPR ratings. A 12f trip on the polytrack is ideal. She’s returning from a 4 month break but was a smart winner last autumn after a similar break. Big player off her current mark.

Kieren O'Neill was very effusive about this filly after an impressive debut where she missed the kick and then produced a sterling finish to cut down a breakaway trip late in the piece on debut. The money was on too. Was all at sea and as green as grass, so with the nearly five months off, will have had considerable experience at getting it right. Strong type who looks set to go places.
One win from 34 is a bit of a concern but stats show that Francesi has been placed in 13 of those races and the grey kept on well off a pound higher last time out.

Three career runs for the 3yo filly, all on the AW, going close in two of her races - good RPR rating last time out. Decent opening handicap mark. Her breeding does suggest she can find improvement now switching to turf.

Bondi Beach is probably going to be more popular than this horse after a very ordinary debut, but there were a few excuses to be offered for that debut failure, not the least of which was drawing wide on a course that favors inside barriers. Was forward for a long way despite that and faded late. Needed the experience, and I'm expecting a much-improved showing this time out.

Lightly raced 4yo. Four runs last year, three decent efforts, only beaten a length in a £36K handicap. Solid return run last month in a 21-runner £39K handicap - nothing went right in the race. Now dropping down from a class 2 into a £5K class 4 contest, still on a decent mark, strong jockey change, and the quick ground could be a big positive.

The 7-year-old mare wasn’t great last year for her new yard, but she was only beaten around a length last August. She ran quite a few nice races as a 4-year-old and 5-year-old, including on quick ground, and her racing mark now is around 20 lb lower. She had a 6-month break, and I’ll take a chance that the trainer has fixed any problems.
Street Life could be on a handy mark at present following a good 2nd off the same rating 50 over C&D 45 days ago.
